extracted.intended_audience: IMLS peer reviewers assigned to the Museums Empowered FY2024 panel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing panel review of Museums Empowered (IMLS) grant applications, including the review criteria (Goals, Implementation, Results), scoring guidance, comment expectations, confidentiality, and conflict-of-interest rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals — alignment with Museums Empowered purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project meet the purpose of the Museums Empowered (ME) funding opportunity to support projects that use the transformative power of professional development and training to generate systemic change within museums of all types and sizes? Does the project meet one of the goals of ME?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should determine how well the applicant aligns with the overall ME purpose and identify the specific ME goal chosen by the applicant. Program goal and objective choices should be identified clearly in the Narrative (see Notice of Funding Opportunity). You do not need to restate each bullet point in comments but these questions should guide assessment of strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 1 — Digital Technology (Objectives 1.1 & 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide museum staff with the skills to integrate digital technology into museum operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective 1.1: Support staff learning and integration of digital communication platforms and social media tools to enhance audience engagement and community outreach. Objective 1.2: Support staff learning and integration of digital tools and services that enhance access to museum collections. Evaluate whether the project clearly targets these objectives and demonstrates appropriate activities, training, and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 2 — Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (Objectives 2.1 & 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support museum staff in providing inclusive and equitable services to people of diverse geographic, cultural, and socioeconomic backgrounds and to individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective 2.1: Create training and learning opportunities that increase cultural competency of museum staff and enhance relevancy of museum programs. Objective 2.2: Develop and implement inclusive and equitable fellowship, internship, and mentoring programs to increase support for emerging professionals from diverse communities entering the museum field. Assess alignment, cultural competence, and how activities will produce equitable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 3 — Evaluation (Objectives 3.1 & 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen the ability of museum staff to use evaluation as a tool to shape museum programs and improve outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective 3.1: Increase staff knowledge of program evaluation methods and the usefulness of evaluation reports, tools, data, and metrics. Objective 3.2: Provide museum staff with the tools and strategies to adapt evaluation methods to address a specific audience or institutional need. Consider whether the project builds evaluation capacity and includes appropriate metrics and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal 4 — Organizational Management (Objectives 4.1 & 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen and support museum staff as the essential part of a resilient organizational culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective 4.1: Develop comprehensive organizational learning opportunities that address one or more emerging priorities facing a museum. Objective 4.2: Develop programs that address the specific learning and growth opportunities identified by staff needs assessments. Evaluate fit with institutional needs and plans for sustaining organizational learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation — project readiness and logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the project poised for successful implementation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the proposal: demonstrates thorough understanding of relevant issues and current practices; addresses an identified need; allocates resources for the successful completion of the project; connects goals and objectives to appropriate activities and intended outcomes. Look for clear work plans, budgets aligned to activities, identified partners/consultants, timelines, and discussion of risks and mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results — feasibility of achieving outcomes and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: If funded, will the project achieve its intended results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the project: tracks, measures, and adapts to achieve desired outcomes; generates continuing benefits for applicant and/or audience served. Review evaluation plans, performance measures, logic models, and plans for continuing activities post-grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Reviewer Comments — one substantive comment per criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For each application you review, write a constructive and substantive comment for each of the panel review criteria: Goals, Implementation, and Results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three areas have equal weight. Comments should justify scores, be prepared objectively based on the application (not prior knowledge of an institution), and complement numeric scores. You may prepare comments offline and paste into eGMS Reach. Review new and resubmitted proposals using the same criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of effective and poor reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes a good vs. poor comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective comments: are presented in a constructive manner; are both substantive and easy to read and understand; reflect the resources of the institution; are specific to the individual application; reflect the numeric score assigned; highlight the application's strengths and identify areas for improvement; are directed to applicants—not IMLS or panel reviewers—for their use. Poor comments: simply summarize or paraphrase the applicant's words; make derogatory remarks; penalize because you feel the institution does not need the money; offer irrelevant information; compare the application to others in the review group; make vague/overly general statements; question an applicant's honesty or integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: What reviewers should NOT consider
rubrics_metrics.description: List of factors outside the scope of ME review criteria that should not influence evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT consider: an institution's financial or staffing needs; whether a project is innovative (ME projects do not need to be innovative); whether a project is new or a resubmission; the size or age of an organization (focus on whether the project is poised for success and aligns with strategy); an institution's indirect cost rate (IMLS honors negotiated rates or accepts 10% in absence of agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias awareness and avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and mitigate common review biases (affinity bias, confirmation bias, conformity bias, contrast effect) to ensure fair evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of tendencies such as favoring those 'like you', focusing on information that confirms prior notions, being swayed by majority or loud voices, or evaluating relative to other applications instead of on its own merits. Examples of biased comments are shown. Pay attention to personal preferences and avoid penalizing sound projects for formatting or spelling errors; evaluate on merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring definitions and assigning an overall score (1–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a single preliminary score for the overall project using a scale of 1 to 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score definitions: 5 = Exceptional (outstanding); 4 = Very Good (solid support); 3 = Good (adequate but could be strengthened); 2 = Some Merit (flawed, inadequate support; could be revised); 1 = Poor (does not fit program goals or provides insufficient information). Use the criteria (Goals, Implementation, Results) to inform an overall score; all three areas have equal weight. Strive for consistency across applications; do not evaluate on a curve. Scores should support and be supported by comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and prohibition on AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant application information is strictly confidential and reviewers must not use AI generative tools to analyze or critique IMLS grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not discuss or reveal names, institutions' project activities, or any application information in person, email, or social media. Because AI tools submit and store substantial information and reviewers cannot control where that information goes, IMLS explicitly prohibits peer reviewers from using AI tools to analyze and critique IMLS grant applications. While funded applications become public record, unfunded applications are not released; reviewer identities are not shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and review process overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural summary from application submission through award announcement that frames reviewers' role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key steps: organizations submit via Grants.gov; IMLS staff check eligibility/completeness; staff identify peer reviewers; peer review occurs (field/panel tiers) and each eligible application typically receives 3–6 reviews; staff assess budgets and past performance for highly ranked applications; staff provide recommended list to IMLS Director; Director makes final decisions; IMLS notifies applicants and provides anonymous copies of reviews to applicants. Reviewers receive notification of awards. Understand that reviewer feedback is used in recommendations and provided to applicants verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, conflicts of interest, and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must comply with government ethics rules and disclose or recuse for conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General principles include placing public trust above private gain, not holding conflicting financial interests, not using nonpublic government information for private gain, avoiding gifts from parties seeking official action, acting impartially, protecting federal property, and adhering to equal opportunity laws. Summary of conflict laws (18 U.S.C. §§201,203,205,207,208,209) is provided. If you believe you may have a conflict (financial, past association, ongoing negotiations, spouse/minor child involvement), notify IMLS immediately and do not review affected applications. Even if no conflict at review time, you may not later represent the applicant to IMLS. Reviewers must certify compliance with the Conflict of Interest Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements: eGMS Reach use, deadlines, and records retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical steps and requirements for reviewers' use of the grants system and handling of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sign in to eGMS Reach via Login.gov and follow job aid instructions. Enter scores and comments in eGMS Reach by the Evaluation Due Date shown in the Panel Information tab. Keep applications and notes confidential and retain copies until August 31, 2024; after that, delete electronic copies and shred paper copies. If you have questions about system access, contact imls-museumreviewers@imls.gov.
